claims.text: A 25 year old man presented to a clinic with frequent stools, fecal incontinence, blood in feces, painful defecation and straining since the past five months, with fluctuating fever, weight loss, lower back pain and pus-like discharge. He was a known case of Hirschsprung disease and ulcerative colitis, had a rectal Duhamel procedure and ten other surgeries, and had three blood transfusions. Examination showed clubbing, pallor, melasma and a fistula with an external opening at the anal verge.

MRI of the pelvis showed rectal and rectosigmoid mural thickening, pre-sacral collections and a linear tract. Sigmoidoscopy showed severe ulcerations, a friable mucosa and fistula openings. A tissue sample from the anorectal junction was taken, and PCR was conducted on the collected sample.

claims.text: Laboratory results included hemoglobin 15.0 g/dL, platelets 534 x10E9/L, ESR 35 mm/hr and CRP 17 mg/L, with negative HIV and AFB testing. After this diagnosis a quadruple regimen of isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol and pyrazinamide was started.
